title: Localizing Memorized Regions in Diffusion Models via Coordinate-Wise Curvature Differences
claim: Our curvature-difference maps recover the memorized region more faithfully than the prior attention-based localization, matching the ground-truth mask.
layout: 2 rows by 8 columns, left-to-right, per-example heatmap strips against ground-truth mask
description: A grid of two rows (two examples) and eight columns with bold column titles. The first three columns show the training image, the generated image, and a black-and-white ground-truth memorization mask. The first example is a living-room scene with a circular wall painting, and the mask is a black disc. The second example has a wide magenta panel above a sofa, and the mask is a black rectangle across the top. The next four columns are grayscale heatmaps for the proposed metrics Δh_∅, Δs_∅, Δh_θ̃ and Δs_θ̃. In these maps the memorized region is dark and the background is bright, so they match the mask closely. The Δs maps are noisier than the Δh maps. The last column is the prior method, Bright Ending, which shows edge-like structure and a blurry, less clean localization. The eye goes first to the mask and then to the heatmap columns.
caption: Qualitative comparison of memorization localization. For each example, we show the training image, the generated image, and the ground-truth memorization mask. We compare the proposed curvature-difference-based metrics ∆h∅(Eq. 1) and ∆h˜θ (Eq. 2), together with their score-difference-based surrogates ∆s∅(Eq. 5) and ∆s˜θ (Eq. 6), against the prior work, Bright Ending (BE) (Chen et al., 2025). Light regions indicate large values and hence high memorization scores.
abstract: Diffusion models can unintentionally memorize training samples, raising concerns about privacy and copyright. While recent methods can detect memorization, they often rely on global or model-specific signals and provide limited insight into where memorization appears within a generated image. We provide a geometric characterization of local memorization as a coordinate-wise variance collapse. However, such collapse can also arise from intrinsic data constraints rather than overfitting. To isolate overfitting-driven memorization, we propose curvature-difference methods that subtract the curvature of an underfitted baseline, either the unconditional model or a less-trained version of itself. We further derive a score-difference proxy that provides a geometric explanation for the widely used score-difference-based detection metric. Experiments on Stable Diffusion, evaluated against ground-truth memorization masks, show that our method outperforms the prior attention-based localization method. Code is available at https://github.com/Gwangho99/mem-curv-diff.
